title: NOV-B1 commit #3: judges and controls (before the first judge call)
system: You are an expert on online one-dimensional bin packing heuristics: textbook rules (First/Best/Worst/Almost-Worst/Next Fit, Harmonic-k, Sum-of-Squares), genetic-programming hyper-heuristics (Burke, Hyde, Kendall), and LLM-evolved heuristics (FunSearch, EoH, ReEvo, HSEvo, MCTS-AHD, LLM4AD, the ab-heuristics of Herrmann & Pallez 2025). You judge whether a priority function decides like a known heuristic.
question:
Harness: priority(item, bins) scores every bin that can hold the item (bins = remaining capacities; unused bins at full capacity are included) and the item goes to the highest score (first index on ties).

Does the CANDIDATE decide like any heuristic you know from the literature, up to tie-breaks or monotone transformations of the score, or is it a member of a published parametric family with other parameters?
Answer with exactly one first line, one of:
KNOWN:<name>
KNOWN_FAMILY_NEW_PARAMETERS:<family>
NOT_KNOWN
DEGENERATE
then one paragraph of justification. DEGENERATE means the rule is trivial or broken (e.g. always opens a new bin, or ignores the bins).
gate_rule: >= 9/10 controls correct; KNOWN controls accept KNOWN or KNOWN_FAMILY_NEW_PARAMETERS

controls.rule: Score combines squared distance of the bin from the largest remaining capacity and powers of bins/item; scores of bins larger than the item are negated, then each score has the previous bin's score subtracted.

If the item leaves a gap of at most 1, pick the tightest such bin; otherwise avoid bins whose gap would be at most 21; among bins leaving a larger gap prefer the one leaving the largest gap, and open a new bin last.
EoH-style closed-form score of bins and item: bins over the square root of log(bins - item), raised to bins/sqrt(item), times exp(item*(bins-item)) and constants.
Place the item in the open bin with the most remaining room; open a new bin only if no open bin fits.
Choose the bin that minimises the resulting sum over gap sizes of the squared number of open bins with that gap.
Prefer the bin whose leftover after placement is closest to the item's own size; new bins only when the item exceeds 70% of capacity.
Score = sin(leftover / 5) plus a small preference for leftovers that are multiples of 7.
Pick the bin whose leftover is closest to the median leftover of all fitting bins.
Prefer leftovers whose ratio to the item is closest to the golden ratio 1.618.
Score = leftover modulo the item size (prefer leftovers that are just below a multiple of the item), ties to the fuller bin.

ctl_eoh: the best-F EoH member, variables renamed (scores->val, bins->caps)
input: candidate code + rule in words from the blind manual read + three nearest corpus heuristics by agreement (name, adapter note, agreement, code)
class_rules: judge class = J1 if J1 == J2 else tiebreak; NOVEL needs NB + judge class NOT_KNOWN + manual read 'no equivalent'; strict variant needs both J1 and J2 NOT_KNOWN; any KNOWN_FAMILY_NEW_PARAMETERS (judge or manual) -> own non-novel class; if fewer than 2 judges pass the gate the judges become advisory, the manual read decides and V3 is flagged 'judge gate unmet'
